name: Central Otago

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

keyfacts: It is the only true continental climate zone in New Zealand, with large daily and seasonal temperature extremes, protected from the maritime climate by high mountains.
Frost can occur at any time between March and November, and heavy frosts are common throughout winter.
The harvest begins in mid to late April, some six to seven weeks later than in the more northerly vineyards.
Soils are rough-edged mica and other metamorphic schists in silt loams that drain easily, so irrigation is generally essential.
The sub-regions include Bannockburn, Bendigo, Tarras, Gibbston, Wānaka, Alexandra Basin and Cromwell Basin, with Gibbston the coolest and highest.

blurb.text: A South Island geographical indication and one of the world's southernmost wine regions. Pinot Noir is its best-known wine and covers about 81% of the vines. Pinot Gris, Chardonnay and Riesling make up most of the rest.
